text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italian president Oscar Luigi Scalfaro summoned a meeting of the government over the emergency situation of the labour market and of the rising unemployment rate. Scalfaro said he wanted to be informed about the situation and he was ready to apply emergency measures (all).

* In an interview, Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano was quoted as saying that the government should no longer listen to hard-left Communist Refoundation party's threatening to withdraw its support, Napolitano said that if RC was to withdraw its support this would not necessarily imply a government crisis, as the majority coalition would then be backed by centre-right Freedom Alliance (Il Messaggero).
* Prime Minister Romano Prodi met Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti and PDS leader Massimo D'Alema but no agreement was reached over planned extra budget and privatisations (all).
* Trade unions reaffirmerd their opposition to cuts in public spending as suggested by a Commission which has been set up to study a reform of Italy's welfare state (all).

* The Italian stock exchange will announce today the new composition of shares in the blue-chip MIB30 index of Italy's top 30 listed companies. The Stock Exchange council said Italian industrial holding HPI-Holding di Partecipazioni Industriali will substitute financial group Gemina in the MIB30 index (all).

* State-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica said it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Britain's General Electric Co Plc to study opportunities for collaboration between their respective defence sector companies, Alenia Difesa and GEC Marconi (all).

* Italian insurance firm Generali posted an 8.8 percent premium income rise to over 11.4 trillion lire in 1996 and said that profits last year were "better" than in 1995 but did not give any figures (all).
* Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) 1996 net profit jumped 15 percent to 89 trillion lire versus 77 trillion lire in 1995 (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
